newsitem.title: USA: Kaczynski relatives say FBI misrepresented comments.
newsitem.headline: Kaczynski relatives say FBI misrepresented comments.

text.p: The mother and brother of Unabomber suspect Theodore Kaczynski say the FBI misrepresented their statements in its request for a warrant to search Kaczynski's cabin, court papers showed on Tuesday.

The declarations from Kaczynski's relatives were attached to a defence motion filed late on Monday that asks a federal judge in Sacramento to throw out all of the evidence seized by the FBI at Kaczynski's Montana cabin in April last year.
The defence maintains the search was illegal because the FBI's affidavit supporting its request for a search warrant contained misleading information.
Another defence motion seeks to throw out statements Kaczynski made to the FBI last April during several hours when he was detained but before he was formally arrested.

Kaczynski, a 54-year-old former mathematics professor, is accused of being the shadowy Unabomber, who killed three people and injured 23 during an anti-technology bombing campaign between 1978 and 1995.

Prosecutors and investigators have said they found extensive evidence at his cabin incriminating Kaczynski, including bomb components and a diary that they say contained his "detailed admission" to each of the 16 Unabomber attacks.
Kaczynski has been charged in Sacramento with four bombings, two of them deadly. He has pleaded not guilty and is scheduled to go on trial in November.
Kaczynski was arrested after his brother David told authorities about his suspicions that he could be the shadowy Unabomber.
But David Kaczynski said in court papers that the FBI misquoted several of his statements in its affidavit seeking a search warrant.

He said he told the FBI that after at first reading a newspaper account of an anti-technology manifesto written by the Unabomber he had "dismissed the possibility" that his brother could be the Unabomber. He denied telling the FBI that after reading the entire manuscript, he was "convinced" his brother was the Unabomber.
In another declaration, Kaczynski's mother Wanda denied saying that the description of the Unabomber fitted her son "but only that he lived alone and was against technology."

"I told the agents that I did not think that Ted was the Unabomber because he hated to travel, he did not like being around people or noise, he did not have a lot of money and he had never been violent," she said.

Kaczynski's lawyers also alleged that, in the search warrant application, the government did not mention that bank records showed Kaczynski was in Montana on Dec. 11, 1985 -- the same day the Unabomber placed a bomb in Sacramento.
They alleged that the government also "misrepresented DNA evidence which if accurately presented would have shown that Kaczynski was excluded" as the Unabomber.
Prosecutors had no comment on the defence motions. They have six weeks to respond in writing. A hearing on the motions is scheduled before U.S. District Judge Garland Burrell in Sacramento on May 16.
